channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani to undergo surgery this week following soccer injury
item.description: "I'm scared; it will be my first surgery," Mamdani said during an unrelated news conference on Monday.

item.title: Trump says he has ordered military to hold off on Iowa explosives detonation for now
item.description: Trump said he wants the OK from the federal appeals court and incoming Iowa governor to proceed.

item.title: 'Deeply shocked': Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher after nude photos used in book campaign
item.description: French feminist icon Gisèle Pelicot, who became a worldwide symbol against sexual violence during the 2024 rape trials against her husband and dozens of other men, said Monday she will take legal action after nude images of her were sent out without her permission to publicise a psychoanalyst's book on coercive control.

item.title: Trump says he 'convinced' Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang
item.description: Jensen Huang has been reinstated as president and CEO of Nvidia.

item.title: WATCH: Celebrating Tom Jackson's extraordinary life and legacy
item.description: The ESPN legend and former All-Pro linebacker died at 75.

item.title: Finland summons Russian ambassador after suspected airspace violation
item.description: Finland on Monday said it had summoned Russia's ambassador over a suspected violation of Finnish airspace by a Russian helicopter and after a Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian cargo ship located in the Gulf of Finland in recent days. Helsinki also condemned Moscow's escalating strikes on civilian targets in Ukraine.

item.title: Airports, public transport shut down amid national strike in Belgium
item.description: Belgium's prime minister on Monday set a new year-end deadline for his coalition government to agree a cost-cutting budget or face collapse. The announcement came as a national strike against the planned cuts grounded all flights in and out of Belgium. Public transport, schools and other public services also faced disruption. France 24's Dave Keating has the latest from Brussels.

item.title: 'Medicare for all' is back on the drawing board. Does it stand a better chance this time?
item.description: Several newly elected Democratic U.S. senators campaigned on Medicare for All. Could this be the time it actually gets traction?

item.title: Iran's courts order US to pay $290 billion in damages
item.description: Iranian courts have ordered the United States to pay $290 billion in damages for decades of US actions against the Islamic Republic, a judiciary official said Monday. He added that lawsuits have also been filed against Gulf Arab states accused of letting Washington use their territory to strike Iran.

item.title: 12,000 evacuated from Don Toliver concert after unknown substance sickens fans
item.description: More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from a concert by American rapper Don Toliver and over 80 were treated by medics after an unknown irritant was released in the crowd, authorities in the English city of Manchester said Monday.

item.title: Behind COP31 failure: A showdown over fossil fuel interests
item.description: Several countries and environmental groups expressed fury at the collapse of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey on Sunday, amid a dramatic failure to thrash out an agreement, two days after the summit was scheduled to end. Oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels – the root cause of the climate crisis – with the EU then refusing to back a weakened text. Our Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.

item.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: Nvidia said on Monday it was reinstating Jensen Huang as ​CEO, effective immediately, an extraordinary reversal that followed calls from US President Donald Trump for his return after Huang resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to have spied for China. France 24's Fraser Jackson has the details.

item.title: Is Cannes mayor David Lisnard a dark horse for French presidential elections?
item.description: French presidential candidate David Lisnard has surprised many by surpassing former prime ministers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal in a recent voter intention pole. The mayor of Cannes is running on an ultra-liberal platform and has gained a large following on social media, but some critics say he lacks the national experience needed for the Elysée.

item.title: Tens of thousands take to streets in Belgium in anti-austerity protests
item.description: Belgium faced a day of political turmoil Monday, as a national strike against planned austerity measures caused widespread disruption, with the government's future hanging in the balance.

item.title: France's socioeconomic crisis: Macron 'trying to impose fiscal discipline on his successor'
item.description: Charli James is pleased to welcome Andrew Smith, Historian of Modern France and Lecturer in Liberal Arts at Queen Mary University of London. He argues that Emmanuel Macron is seeking to "impose fiscal discipline on his successor as president" after "presiding over quite a substantial deterioration in the public finances." For Smith, the difficulty is that "it's easier to agree on the need for fiscal discipline than on who should pay for it or should have the authority to actually determine it." He suggests that the far right "may play the deciding role" in whether the proposal succeeds, potentially presenting itself as "solving the problems created by Macron's two terms."

item.title: Trump claims credit as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
item.description: President Trump endorsed the announcement, calling it essential for the success of the company and the economy. He added that the government does not see Jensen's return as a national security risk.

item.title: Dhaka bursting at the seams: Bangladeshi capital faces public health, housing crisis
item.description: The Bangladeshi capital Dhaka is one of the most densely populated places on Earth, with over 35,000 people per square kilometre, compared with 20,000 in Paris. Every year, 400,000 people from across Bangladesh move to the city. Its rapid and unplanned growth is triggering a crisis in housing, transport and public health. FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Gohin and Navodita Kumari report.

item.title: Ukraine claims strikes on Russian ships off Libyan coast
item.description: Ukraine claimed responsibility on Monday for attacks on two Russian vessels off the coast of Libya the previous day. Here is what we know about the operation, claimed by President Volodymyr Zelensky shortly after the United Nations called for an investigation into the strikes.

item.title: Restaurateur and sister cleared of murdering their 100-year-old mother
item.description: A restaurateur and his sister have been cleared of murdering their 100-year-old mother with morphine.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: PAMELA bring a little light to darker times with 'Dancing on the Edge'
item.description: In this arts24 music show, Jennifer Ben Brahim chats with PAMELA, a Franco-British duo flying the flag for cross-channel friendship. Sam Sprent and Simon Quénéa blend British wit with French flair, carving out a distinctive electro-post-punk sound of their own. They've just released their debut album "Dancing on the Edge", an impassioned call to embrace life to the fullest, even when the world beyond feels dark and uncertain. The record features a collaboration with long-time friend Zaho de Sagazan, one of France's biggest music stars.

item.title: Democrats vow probe after Trump admits role in Huang's return as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Nvidia on ⁠Monday said it ​was immediately reinstating disgraced tech titan Jensen Huang as its chief executive, marking an extraordinary reversal ​under pressure from US President Donald Trump, who said he had intervened with Nvidia's board. Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer vowed to investigate potential wrongdoing by "anybody selling out our national security for financial gain".

item.title: Ukraine sending the message that 'we can attack you where we want'
item.description: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday, claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day. With the attack, as well as the fact that Kyiv has claimed responsibility, Ukraine is sending the message to Russia that "we can attack you where we want", says France 24's James Andre.

item.title: ‘Worst possible choice’: Should date of French election be changed?
item.description: France is set to head to the polls in 2027 for a two-round presidential election, but the choice of the dates of the vote is causing controversy. The ballot is currently set for the 18th of April and the 2nd of May, meaning the vote for the second round will come a day after International Workers' Day, typically a day of protest in the country.

item.title: WATCH: NFL Sunday’s biggest moments
item.description: “GMA” has highlights from the San Francisco 49ers-Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs-Arizona Cardinals games, plus a preview of Monday night's Cincinnati Bengals-Washington Commanders matchup.

item.title: Capita shares at 35-year low as firm counts cost of civil service pension failures
item.description: Capita shares plunged more than 70% on Monday after the UK-based outsourcer revealed plans for a cash call amid an expected slump in profits linked to its troubled Civil Service pension scheme contract.

item.title: Photographer Federico Veronesi: 'I've been in love with African wildlife since I was three'
item.description: The winner of this year's Wildlife Photographer of the Year award has told FRANCE 24 that his winning picture reveals a lot about the complexity of an elephant's soul and feelings. At first glance the image seems to show a mother elephant playing with her calf, but in fact it is a female carrying another elephant's dead calf. Photographer Federico Veronesi told us how he fell in love in Kenya as a six-year-old child and ended up moving there to fulfil his photography dream. He spoke to us in Perspective.

item.title: 'Out of control': ICE agents make arrests at Seattle airport in 'horrific' scene
item.description: The governor of Washington state called US federal immigration agents "out of control" after they arrested two people at Seattle's main airport on Saturday. ICE officers have conducted raids across the United States, part of President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown which has forged ahead despite a rebuke by voters at this month's midterms.

item.title: FBI's national crime database targeted in hack, Trump says
item.description: President Donald Trump confirmed on Saturday that the FBI’s National Crime Information Center database was targeted in a hack.

item.title: Iran live updates: Iranian attacks spike over past week, Trump says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: ‘Fighting for love’: Thousands turn out for Rio Pride parade
item.description: Thousands of people flocked to Copacabana Beach in Rio Sunday for the 31st annual Pride Parade. The event marked 15 years since Brazil's Supreme Court unanimously recognized same sex unions. Ophelie Jacobson explains what the celebration means for the LGBT community this year.

item.title: Thousands protest Turkey media crackdown in Istanbul
item.description: Several thousand people marched through Istanbul on Sunday to protest a growing crackdown on opposition and independent media outlets days after police raided pro-opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV, installing a government-appointed trustee and arresting senior staff members.

item.title: Martin Property Group makes last-gasp pitch to seal Poundland rescue
item.description: The Northern Irish company which has been attempting to seal a solvent rescue of Poundland for more than six weeks has made a last-gasp plea to its owner to engage in talks on a deal which could save thousands of high street jobs.

item.title: Dems holding 12 debates in 2028 cycle, requiring candidates denounce 'dark money'
item.description: The Democratic National Committee announced on Monday that it will hold 12 primary debates in the 2028 presidential primary cycle.

item.title: Papers discuss James Bond's soft power and the next Bond girl
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, November 23: Papers react to the breakdown of the COP31 climate talks. Israeli paper Haaretz reports on the struggles of crossing the Qalandiyah checkpoint. The New York Times talks about the mathematical "formula to stop the apocalypse". Finally, the Bond universe keeps making headlines.

item.title: Ukrainian drones sink Russian warship at naval base in Libya
item.description: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day. Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made sea drones in the operation, which struck what was one of Russia’s newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbour.

item.title: Deadly fire at confectionery factory kills 24 as rescuers search for dozens still missing
item.description: A deadly fire that tore through a confectionery factory in Indonesia has claimed the lives of 24 people, with 34 others still missing.

item.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
item.description: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault.

item.title: Seniors embrace Tesla automated driving technology despite questions about safety
item.description: Older drivers are using Tesla's automated driving technology to stay on the road longer. But safety experts warn the company may be over-selling what its cars can do.

item.title: Mushroom supplements promise health benefits. What does the science say?
item.description: Wellness influencers say mushroom supplements can help with your gut health, focus and immune system. Here is where research suggests there are some links.

item.title: K is for kindness, but families worry the world has less of it
item.description: A decade after first asking families about kindness, Sesame Workshop asked parents similar questions. They responded that their kids are getting kinder even as the wider world becomes less so.

item.title: Let's talk turkey: Here's how Thanksgiving meal costs have changed this year
item.description: Grocery costs have been on the rise, but food-price analysts say it's unclear if you'll spend more on the Thanksgiving meal this year. Some people are deciding not to host or are hosting fewer guests.

item.title: Snow forecast as cold health alerts in parts of UK
item.description: Wintry conditions are set for parts of the UK in the coming days, with snow, frost and sub-zero temperatures forecast.

item.title: Hacker sentenced for leaking Grand Theft Auto VI clips
item.description: A man who hacked into the makers of Grand Theft Auto and leaked clips after stealing 90 gameplay videos from the sixth installment has been sentenced.

item.title: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly
item.description: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible.

item.title: Major trial to examine if AI can help detect breast cancer earlier
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of women taking part in the NHS breast cancer screening programme could have their scans assessed by AI to see if it leads to earlier diagnosis.

item.title: Democrat Chuck Hubbard wins recount, flips North Carolina US House seat
item.description: Democratic Chuck Hubbard will win the election in North Carolina's 5th congressional district, the Associated Press projects.

item.title: Rahm Emanuel: Schumer should commit to stepping down as leader after next Congress
item.description: Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, joined "This Week" to discuss what Democrats should do after their historic midterm victory.

item.title: DNI Clayton: Putin is 'not America's friend in Ukraine'
item.description: The director of national intelligence appeared on ABC's "This Week" Sunday.

item.title: Man who was lured to remote villa and held for 15 hours rescued after being tied up and beaten
item.description: A man has been rescued after he was lured to an isolated villa, held for 15 hours, tied to a chair, beaten, and threatened with death, police in Spain say.

item.title: Suspect charged over death of man found injured in hospital car park
item.description: A suspect has been charged following the death of a young man who was found seriously injured in a hospital car park, almost 20 miles from where he was wounded.

item.title: Meet the Ukrainian energy workers dodging drones to bring people's electricity back
item.description: "The first thing the guys and I do is look at where we can hide."

item.title: At least 11 dead after suspected cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro' captured in Mexico
item.description: An outburst of violence has killed at least 11 people after Mexican authorities captured suspected cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro.

item.title: WATCH: Tips for hosting Friendsgiving this year
item.description: Digital creator Kerra Masella shares her tips for planning and hosting a Friendsgiving celebration, from getting organized ahead of time to making friends feel welcome around the table.

item.title: WATCH: Is travel insurance worth it after the FAA ground stop?
item.description: Katy Nastro, travel correspondent at Flighty, shares what travelers can do to protect themselves.

item.title: Trump touts relationships with Putin and Xi after historic Asia trip
item.description: Trump said the three countries made strides in advancing denuclearization talks.

item.title: WATCH: New health warning on doomscrolling: What to know and tips to break the habit
item.description: A Lancet Psychiatry report calls problematic internet use a global health concern, affecting more than 1 in 10 people. ABC News’ Dr. Jennifer Miao explains the impact and how to protect yourself.

item.title: WATCH: Reporter goes undercover as porch pirate
item.description: A New York Times reporter went undercover as a porch pirate to help identify the best ways to keep your home and packages safe as package deliveries ramp up this holiday season.

item.title: WATCH: Riverboat captain celebrates more than 50 years on the Mississippi River
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to riverboat captain Robbie Mitchell, who is marking a major milestone aboard the legendary steamboat Natchez.

item.title: WATCH: New video angle shows moment of Brooklyn apartment building's deadly collapse
item.description: Dash cam video from a bus passing by shows the terrifying moment a three-story Brooklyn apartment building buckled and crumbled to the ground, killing eight people and injuring multiple others.

item.title: WATCH: Grand Theft Auto VI is back and shattering records
item.description: The excitement around the release of GTA VI is causing gamers to “call out sick” to play and has lit up Miami in Vice City colors. ABC News’ Ashan Singh dives into what the hype is all about.

item.title: Trump China trip: Iran and Ukraine not in 'peace declaration' and more takeaways
item.description: Trump heads back to Washington after meeting with Xi and Putin -- the first sitdown between the three superpowers -- with no tangible diplomatic breakthroughs in hand.

item.description: There are three other former soldiers who are on the military’s death row.

item.description: Doug Lute, former U.S. ambassador to NATO, says President Donald Trump referring to Putin and Xi as friends is "concerning for America's allies."

item.description: Actor Kel Mitchell shares how he's using his star power to help families in need.

item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman in Oregon who helped reunite a missing cat with its owner in South Carolina.
